text: dsh-veripipe（DSH 插件，通用客户端）：为每轮会话生成结束回执，并提供只读工具查看。它注册会话投影，在每次 turn/end 记录待办完成计数、目标标识、结束原因和完成判定；新一轮开始时旧回执仍可读取，最多保留最近 50 条。适合需要在轮次之间核对任务是否完成的 DSH 用户。无需 API 密钥或额外配置。

dsh-veripipe (DSH plugin, any client) stores each turn’s todo counts, goal identity, end reason, and completion verdict in a session projection. A read-only tool retrieves up to 50 receipts that persist across turns, helping check task completion. No API key or extra configuration is required.
想在下一轮开始后仍能查到上一轮的待办完成情况。
需要按轮次读取会话结束时的完成判定和待办统计。
I need to retrieve a session turn’s completion status after the next turn has started.
dsh-veripipe 的「轮次完成回执」功能：在每次 turn/end 时记录该轮的结束原因、待办计数、目标标识和完成判定，并跨后续轮次保留。通过会话投影自动生成，每个会话最多保留最近 50 条回执。
dsh-veripipe 的「读取回执」功能：调用 veripipe_receipt 工具查看当前会话最近的回执，可用 limit 指定数量（默认 1，范围 1 到 50），并返回回执内容及可用、已返回数量。
dsh-veripipe 的维护与更新元数据：活跃维护；距最后推送 35 天；提交数 2；更新频次 unknown；近 90 天提交 未知；开放 Issue 未知；仓库健康分 62/100（置信度 low）。

dsh-veripipe README · dsh-veripipe：A [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) (dsh) plugin that mints a **turn-terminal receipt** for every turn and keeps it readable after the turn ends — plus a read-only tool to read receipts back. It adds no model calls, no network, and no writes to your session.

dsh-veripipe README · The problem it solves：dsh ships a `todos` session projection that an agent updates with `todo_write`. That projection is **cleared on every `turn/start`**: once the next turn begins, reading the `todos` projection returns `null`. An external verifier that inspects a session *between* turns therefore cannot tell a plan that finished (all todos `completed`) from one that was abandoned — both read as "no list".

dsh-veripipe README · The problem it solves：`dsh-veripipe` folds the same event log into a parallel projection whose entries are **never cleared by a later turn**. At each `turn/end` it records one receipt capturing that turn's terminal state, so the completion status of every turn stays readable for the life of the session.

dsh-veripipe README · What it registers：- **`veripipeReceipts` session projection** — a pure, deterministic fold over the session event log (`turn/start`, `todo/write`, `goal/change`, `turn/end`). It mints one receipt per `turn/end` and keeps the newest 50. It replays from the log like any other projection; it stores no state of its own outside the event stream.
- **`veripipe_receipt` tool** — read-only. Returns the current session's most recent receipts (default 1). It performs no model call, no network request, and no writes.

dsh-veripipe README · Install：```sh
dsh plugin --profile <your-profile> add github:zhangyy0423/dsh-veripipe
```

The repository ships prebuilt output (`lib/`) and has no `prepare` script, so nothing is built on install. It is not published to npm. A local checkout or a packed tarball also works:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile <your-profile> add ./dsh-veripipe          # local checkout
dsh plugin --profile <your-profile> add ./dsh-veripipe-0.1.0.tgz # from `npm pack`
```

dsh-veripipe README · Install：All `@deepseek-ai/*` packages are **peer dependencies** supplied by the host dsh installation; the plugin declares them as peers (not regular dependencies) on purpose. Declaring them as dependencies would load a second copy of `@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools` and break every tool call. `zod` is the only direct runtime dependency.

dsh-veripipe README · Receipt fields：| Field | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `turn` | integer | The turn number this receipt certifies (`-1` if the event omitted it). |
| `endReason` | string | The `turn/end` reason kind (e.g. `completed`, `aborted`, `error`); `unknown` if unreadable. |
| `todos` | object \| null | Counts of the last todo list written in the turn: `{ total, completed, inProgress, pending }`, or `null` if none was written. |
| `goal` | object \| null | Goal identity at turn end: `{ id, phase, revision }`, or `null` if no goal was active. |
| `verdict.planComplete` | `pass` \| `fail` \| `inconclusive` | The fail-closed completion judgement (below). |

dsh-veripipe README · Verdict semantics (fail-closed)：The verdict is deliberately conservative — uncertainty is never reported as `pass`:

- **`pass`** — a non-empty todo list was written this turn **and every item is `completed`**.
- **`fail`** — a non-empty todo list was written **and at least one item is not `completed`**.
- **`inconclusive`** — no todo list was written this turn, the list was empty, or the `todo/write` payload was unreadable.

dsh-veripipe README · Tool usage：```jsonc
// veripipe_receipt (no required arguments)
{ "limit": 3 }   // optional; how many of the most recent receipts to return, newest last.
                 // Defaults to 1; clamped to 1..50.
```

Returns:

```jsonc
{
  "available": 7,            // total receipts kept for this session
  "returned": 3,             // how many this call returned
  "receipts": [              // oldest first

Before the first turn ends, the tool returns `{ "available": 0, "returned": 0, "receipts": [] }`.

dsh-veripipe README · Privacy：Receipts store **counts and identifiers only**. The fold never records prompts, todo text, tool arguments, tool results, or a goal's objective text — only per-status todo counts, the goal's `id`/`phase`/`revision`, the turn number, and the end-reason kind. The `veripipe_receipt` tool returns exactly those fields and nothing more.

dsh-veripipe README · Relation to veripipe：[`veripipe`](https://github.com/zhangyy0423/veripipe) is an external verification pipeline that judges whether an agent actually completed the task it was given. Its dsh adapter reads a session's state after the run. Because the stock `todos` projection is cleared at the next `turn/start`, a between-turns read cannot distinguish a finished plan from an abandoned one. This plugin closes that gap on the dsh side: it exposes a durable, fail-closed, counts-only completion signal per turn that such a verifier can read without re-deriving history or touching private content. The plugin is independently useful without veripipe — it is a general turn-completion ledger — and is maintained separately from the harness.

dsh-veripipe README · Development：```sh
DSH_HARNESS=/path/to/deepseek-harness bash scripts/link-harness.sh  # dev links for type-checking
npm run build   # tsc -p tsconfig.json -> lib/
npm test        # node --test over the pure fold (tests/*.test.mjs)
```

`lib/` is committed so installs need no build; rebuild and commit it after changing `src/`.

The whole computation lives in `src/receipt.ts`, which imports nothing from the harness and is unit-tested in isolation against the compiled `lib/receipt.js`.
